Subject: HearthHealth discovery — alignment & mutual plan

Hi Lynn / Rajiv —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

Pain points confirmed:
- Latency spikes on patient triage flows during morning batch windows (~200–400ms spikes) that degrade throughput for real-time triage.
- High per-token inference cost for summary/triage models when traffic bursts — this limits model iteration.
- Compliance requirement: audit logs + customer data residency for PHI-adjacent metadata.

Goals you shared:
1) Reduce 95th percentile latency to <90ms for 1–2 critical endpoints.
2) Cut inference cost per request by ~25% while keeping quality within current threshold.
3) Have an auditable trail and an option for private deployment in Q1 2027 if needed.

What we propose (high level):
- Pilot with our Dedicated capacity (small reserved GPU pool) to validate latency and throughput under your morning window.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for the triage model and apply a quantization profile to reduce per-token cost.
- Provide an SOC2/architecture packet + optional VPC private control plane for residency/audit testing.

Immediate next steps (owner in parens):
- Redwood to deliver Mutual Action Plan (MPA) draft with milestones and owners by 10/07 (marissa_cole).
- HearthHealth to share primary procurement contact and technical SRE by 10/08 (Lynn).
- Schedule a short technical sync (30m) to validate expected sequence lengths and traffic profile — propose 10/13 or 10/14 (ben_carter / david_kim to coordinate).

Attachments I’ll send in the next email: MPA draft, initial SOW template, and a suggested demo agenda.

Thanks — we’re excited to move this forward.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

- Commercial/contract issues escalate to Elena + marissa_cole.
